summary: Tulku Sherdor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, and learned under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup (1939–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (1920–1996) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Karsé Kongtrul, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.
Tuomo Pekkanen is a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied under Pentti Aalto around 1953–1968 and held a post at the University of Jyväskylä circa 1972–1998.

Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology. He earned his degrees from the University of Washington, studying under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche. He served at the University of Washington as Associate Professor (1958) and Professor (1970).
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute (attested 2008, 2019) and under traditional teachers Tashi Wangchuk (2003–2004), Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen (2005), and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (attested 2019).
Tyler M. Richard is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held a post in South Asian Studies at Harvard University and was attested as faculty at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Tzungkuen Wen specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Queensland (-2009) and studied under several teachers. He was Lecturer at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (2005) and Head of Counseling and Guidance at Chung-Hwa Institute (attested 2026).
U-tain Wongsathit specializes in Indology and linguistics. He earned a Ph.D. in Sanskrit from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2010 and held a post at Silpakorn University in 2003.

U. Ghimire works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Nepal Sanskrit University (-2023) and degrees in public health. His posts include Program Coordinator at Rambadevi College (2012–2015) and Public Health Professional for the Government of Nepal (2017).
U. V. Swaminatha Iyer (1855–1942) was an Indology scholar. He held posts at Pachaiyappa's College (~1903–1919) and Annamalai University (~1932–1936).

Udaya Narayana Singh is a linguist who earned his degrees at the University of Calcutta and University of Delhi. His posts include Professor at University of Hyderabad (1987–2000), Director of CIIL (2000–2009), and Dean at Amity University, Gurugram (2017).

Udo Posch (1922–1965) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1945–1949) under Robert Bleichsteiner and Herbert W. Duda. He held posts at the University of Graz (1952) and University of Washington (1953).
Ugyen Pelgen works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a master's degree at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ujjwal Kumar specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he served as Assistant Professor (2006–2016), before becoming a Professor at the University of Calcutta in 2016.

Ulrich Mammitzsch (1935–1990) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Hamburg, SIU Carbondale, and Hawaiʻi (Ph.D. ~1961–1968). He held posts at University of Hawaiʻi and Western Washington University (Director of East Asian Studies, 1971).

Ulrich Pagel works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme (attested 1995). In 1999, he was appointed Seiyi Kiriyama Professor in Buddhist Studies at SOAS University of London.

Ulrich Schneider (1922–1992) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller. He held posts at Leipzig (1957), Freiburg (PD 1959; Professor 1964–1980), and Münster (Professor 1980–1987).

Ulrich Timme Kragh specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying at KIBI and the University of Copenhagen. He held posts at Copenhagen, Geumgang University (2008–2010), Harvard (2004–2007), and visiting fellowships at Sydney (2014–2015) and ANU (2015).
